title: Cache shipping rates that many checkouts read at once

blocks.text: The shop's checkout asks for a shipping rate on every basket, hundreds of times a second, and the rates change a few times a day. `RateCache` keeps them in memory behind a `ReentrantReadWriteLock`. The tariff job's `replace` is already written. What's missing is the read: answer from the cache, and on a zone that isn't cached yet, ask the slow rates service once, keep the answer and return it.

Write `rateFor` in `src/main/java/practice/RateCache.java`. Checkouts must be able to read rates side by side without waiting for each other, and a miss must load the rate without stopping the cache. About twelve lines.
The tests make each call from a thread of their own, and hold the read lock themselves to stand in for a checkout that is in the middle of a read.

cases.says: rates the tariff job set are answered from the cache, including a replaced one, without calling the rates service
a zone that isn't cached is loaded from the rates service, kept, and answered from the cache the next time
a checkout gets a cached rate while another checkout is in the middle of a read

origin.section: A Read-Write Lock Lets Readers Share, but a Reader Can't Upgrade

concepts: A thread holding the read lock that asks for the write lock waits for itself forever, and new readers and writers queue behind it; release the read lock first, and downgrading is allowed.
Any number of threads can hold a read lock together, while the write lock excludes readers and writers.
